chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) freed a Christian slave of his, and he embraced Islam at the time he was freed.
Because he (peace be upon him) only freed him due to his knowledge that when he freed him, he would embrace Islam.
As for one who does not know that from him, it is not permissible for him to free the disbeliever, according to what the first report contained.

And when a man frees his slave or his female slave, and another has a share in her with him, he is obliged to buy what remains and free her if he is wealthy; and if he is poor, the slave is asked for what remains.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a non-Muslim slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle that freeing a non-Muslim slave (*kafir*) is valid and recommended if the owner knows the slave will convert to Islam, as demonstrated by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) freeing a Christian slave. It further details the procedural requirement for partial owners to buy out their partner's share to effect full emancipation, distinguishing between the obligations of the wealthy and the accommodation for the poor through installment payments.
